newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Anderson says no bailout for CAI.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Anderson says no bailout for CAI.

text.p: Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson said on Wednesday there was no room for a government bailout of troubled carrier Canadian Airlines Corp.
He said the only way to save the airline was to proceed with a restructuring plan proposed by the company's management.

"We have little choice at the moment but to continue with the restructuring plan that Mr. Benson has proposed and we have joined in with," Anderson told reporters after a meeting with Canadian's chief executive Kevin Benson and Canadian Auto Workers union president Buzz Hargrove.
The meeting, which took place in Anderson's Ottawa office, lasted about 20 minutes and produced no result.
"We know that this cannot be a government bailout of a company that has chronic losses. We know there must be restructuring," Anderson said.
The minister said it was now up to Hargrove and his union to embrace the restructuring plan or watch the airline come close to collapse.

"We are at a stage now that we are imploring Mr. Hargrove of the CAW, after intense negotiations all last week, to do the right thing which is to let his membership vote on the deal just like the members of the other unions in the Canadian family," Anderson said.
Earlier Hargrove said he would not allow CAW members to vote on the plan.
All five other unions at Canadian have given their support for the company's restructuring scheme, as have Ottawa and the provincial governments of Alberta and British Columbia.

AMR Corp, the parent of American Airlines, which has a 33 percent stake and a 25 percent voting interest in Canadian, has also agreed to cut its service fees by C$48 million a year to support the restructuring. ((Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau, 613-235-6745))
